newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Range-bound NZ debt ends a fraction stronger.
newsitem.headline: Range-bound NZ debt ends a fraction stronger.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
* NZ debt markets end marginally stronger after dead day
* Dealers look to employment data for direction
New Zealand yields ended steady on Wednesday after another directionless, volume-less session.
The 90-day bank bills closed two points stronger at 7.38 percent, after edging higher at the open to 7.43 percent.

Dealers said the currency's Trade-Weighted Index had played dictator once more, prompting early weakness in the bills when it slipped to 68.58, and a rally back when it regained the lost ground and bounced back to around 68.80.
"Seriously, it hasn't traded this afternoon," one bill dealer said of the lack of flows.

He said the next market driver would be the Quarterly Employment Survey next Tuesday. Others have suggested this Friday's Labour Cost Index data may have the potential to spark the flagging market back to life.

Meanwhile, bonds finished largely flat, with the long bonds a couple of points stronger at 7.28 percent. Dealers said technical signals across the yield curve were mixed as the range-bound market struggled to find short-term direction.
